https://github.com/sindresorhus/got/compare/v16.1.0...v16.2.0

This release is the result of a large bug hunt. Many of the fixes make Got match its documented behavior, so you may notice some of them:

- Invalid options now throw: an empty `method`, a negative or fractional `maxRedirects` or `retry.limit`, a `prefixUrl` with a query string or fragment, and a `handlers` entry that is not a function.
- A stream with a `body`, `json`, or `form` option now rejects writes, as documented.
- The promise `response` event now only fires for the final response, not for every retry attempt.
- `got.extend({body})` (and `json`, `form`) no longer sends the payload with every request of the instance. Payloads are never merged with defaults.
- `instance.extend()` now inherits the parent's `mutableDefaults`, like `got.extend(instance)`.
- A `HEAD` request is no longer changed to `GET` on a `301`, `302`, or `303` redirect.
- `response.body` no longer keeps a leading UTF-8 byte order mark, and JSON with a byte order mark now parses.

## Improvements

- Accept number values in `headers`  6fffc9e
- Export the `Timings`, `DnsCacheLookup`, and `DnsCacheOptions` types  d012d1d eccaaca
- Retry `FormData` bodies by re-serializing them instead of failing  90c6ec1
- Support the `x-gzip` content coding and stacked content codings  5550a79

- Fix `Infinity` timeouts firing at once or throwing  724ebc2
- Fix retry delay edge cases, including invalid `Retry-After` values and `calculateDelay` for `afterResponse` retries  fe58b8c 0193605
- Fix retries with replaced or non-replayable bodies  ae5521f 7c1cda3 8bbc79f 1a56d36 d012d1d
- Fix the default `paginate` on real-world `Link` headers, and several pagination option and limit edge cases  bd2dee0 1e61807 602b179 f98d0e1 c8419e4 526a988 557e61f 4712e5b a4a50ad b65e533
- Fix `afterResponse`, `beforeRequest`, and `beforeCache` hook edge cases  45c201c c1cf0f8 850e49b a4a50ad 863cf30 494279b
- Fix response body decoding and parsing edge cases  c36ad51 c409a84 3c6eaf1 f658d3e dbd83df
- Fix stream edge cases: respect backpressure, stop forwarding after unpipe, and do not copy hop-by-hop headers to a piped `ServerResponse`  348e114 dc929bd dc56e4b c930cd9 a9a754f
- Fix uploads: `DataView` byte ranges, upload error classification, progress `total` for `Content-Length: 0`, and cancelling Web `ReadableStream` bodies  2a66686 d1cb051 0238069 b57120c 200bc85
- Fix option normalization, cloning, and immutable defaults  8f44d81 687eb7d 30023f7 5548b00 bec5da6 bcc0b01 9348ad6 a9a754f 7b13369 3bd0486 d272656 0e537c7 60b62a0 129d88d

### Introducing Got v12.0.0 :tada:

Long time no see! The latest Got version (v11.8.2) was released just in February ❄️ 
We have been working hard on squashing bugs and improving overall experience.

If you find Got useful, you might want to [sponsor the Got maintainers](https://github.com/sindresorhus/got?sponsor=1).

### This package is now pure ESM

**Please [read this](https://gist.github.com/sindresorhus/a39789f98801d908bbc7ff3ecc99d99c).** Also see https://github.com/sindresorhus/got/issues/1789.

- **Please don't open issues about `[ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]` and `Must use import to load ES Module` errors.** This is a problem with your setup, not Got.
- Please don't open issues about using Got with Jest. Jest does not fully support ESM.
- Pretty much any problem with loading this package is a problem with your bundler, test framework, etc, not Got.
- If you use TypeScript, you will want to stay on Got v11 until TypeScript 4.6 is out. [Why.](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/46452)
- If you use a bundler, make sure it supports ESM and that you have correctly configured it for ESM.
- The Got issue tracker is not a support channel for your favorite build/bundler tool.

### Required Node.js >=14

While working with streams, we encountered more Node.js bugs that needed workarounds.
In order to keep our code clean, we had to drop Node.js v12 as the code would get more messy.
We strongly recommend that you update Node.js to **v14 LTS**.

### HTTP/2 support

Every Node.js release, the native `http2` module gets more stable.
Unfortunately there are still some issues on the Node.js side, so we decided to keep HTTP/2 disabled for now.
We may enable it by default in Got v13. It is still possible to turn it on via the `http2` option.

To run HTTP/2 requests, it is required to use Node.js **v15.10** or above.

```

```

*The release notes will be improved in the final v11 release.*

Changes in beta 1:

### Breaking

##### API

- `options.encoding` will no longer affect streams (reverting back to the Got 9 behavior), use `got.stream(…).setEncoding(encoding)` instead (to prevent confusion).
- Renamed `GotError` to `RequestError`.
- `options.agent` can no longer be an instance of `http.Agent`. Instead you need to pass:
```js
{
	http: new http.Agent(…),
	https: new https.Agent(…),
	http2: new http2wrapper.Agent(…)
}
```
- The deprecated `useElectronNet` option has been removed.
- `dnsCache` is now enabled by default.
- `dnsCache` no longer can be a Map or a Keyv instance, instead you need to pass a [CacheableLookup](https://github.com/szmarczak/cacheable-lookup) instance.
- Errors thrown in `init` hooks will be converted to `RequestError`s (why: `RequestError` provides much more useful information (e.g. Got options) than the usual TypeError etc.).
- `options._pagination` has been renamed to `options.pagination`.
- The `options.url` property will no longer be visible in `init` hooks (design limitation).
- The `error.request` property is no longer a `ClientRequest` instance. Instead, it gives a Got stream.

##### Types

- The `ResponseObject` type has been merged into the `Response` type.
- Renamed the `Defaults` type to `InstanceDefaults`.
- Renamed the `DefaultOptions` type to `Defaults`.
- Renamed the `DefaultRetryOptions` type to `RequiredRetryOptions`.
- Renamed the `GotOptions` type to `Options`.
- Renamed the `GotRequestMethod` type to `GotRequestFunction`.
